citation_details.title: Integrated Synergetic Theory (TSI): Phase Signature, Information Thermodynamics, and Exploratory Empirical Validation via EEG Hyperscanning
citation_details.author: Eduardo Andres Garcia Lecaros
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: The Transferred Potential phenomenon, first reported by Grinberg-Zylberbaum et al. (1994), posits the existence of instantaneous electroencephalographic correlations between electromagnetically isolated brains. Existing quantum and classical frameworks leave open the question of how such a channel could filter signal-specific information from background neural noise. This work formalizes the Integrated Synergetic Theory (TSI), introducing a Phase Signature authentication protocol ($ID_{AB}$) derived from prior interactions between neural nodes, within a thermodynamic information framework bounded by the Landauer limit. The model predicts: (1) local entropy reduction at the receiver ($\Delta S_B < 0$), (2) elevated inter-brain mutual information $I(A:B)$ during active pairing, (3) inter-brain phase coherence exceeding baseline, and (4) a thermodynamic work balance $\Delta F_B \approx W_{\text{ext}} = k_B T \cdot I(A{:}B)\ln 2$. As an exploratory empirical evaluation, these predictions were tested against real hyperscanning EEG data from the OpenNeuro public repository (dataset ds007822, Prisoner's Dilemma paradigm, $N = 1$ dyad, 19 channels, $f_s = 300$ Hz). Using z-score normalization per channel and epoch, 4th-order Butterworth bandpass filtering in the theta band (4–8 Hz), and inter-brain Phase Locking Value (PLV) computed across all 361 channel pairs, two of the four quantitative predictions were confirmed: entropy reduction ($\Delta S_B = -0.049$ nats) and higher mutual information in the paired condition ($I_{\text{paired}} = 0.475$ bits vs. $I_{\text{control}} = 0.470$ bits). Inter-brain theta PLV did not reach statistical significance ($U = 680$, $p = 0.66$), consistent with the statistical power limitations of a single-dyad analysis. The primary theoretical gap remains the formal demonstration of compatibility with the quantum No-Communication Theorem. All analysis code and data pipelines are provided for full reproducibility.

citation_details.title: Brain Topography Null-Calibrated Hyperscanning Analysis
citation_details.author: Chang S. Nam, Heegyu Kim
citation_details.abstract: Initial public release of the analysis code and frozen reference outputs for: Simulation-Informed Progressive Null Calibration of Inter-Brain PLV Topographies in Triadic Cooperation This release includes the four-layer null-calibration pipeline, ground-truth simulation, within-triad dyad null, iCOH robustness analysis, triad-level stability analyses, frozen manuscript evidence, and manuscript figure-generation code. Associated public EEG dataset: OpenNeuro ds007822.
